identity.title: Ascites exam: flank dullness, shifting dullness, fluid wave

technique.how: Supine: percuss from the tympanitic umbilical area toward each flank; dullness in the flanks (flank dullness) is the screening sign. If present, mark the border, roll the patient laterally, wait ~30 s and re-percuss for shift. Fluid wave: assistant presses hand edge on midline; tap one flank and feel for a transmitted impulse on the opposite flank.
technique.prerequisites: Supine, relaxed abdomen; bladder emptied; assistant for fluid wave.
technique.contraindications: None specific; avoid rolling patients with spinal instability or fresh wounds.

interpretation.positive_finding: Fluid wave (LR+ 9.6) and shifting dullness (LR+ 5.76) each raise the probability of ascites several-fold; a fluid wave in a patient with prolonged PT has a positive predictive value near 96%.
interpretation.negative_finding: No flank dullness is the most reliable single negative: Cattau found it the only manoeuvre with >90% accuracy for concluding ascites is absent. Absent bulging flanks has LR- 0.12.
interpretation.pitfalls: Small-volume ascites (<1-1.5 L) is often missed; obesity, ovarian cysts, distended bowel and pregnancy mimic or mask signs; in low-prevalence patients (normal PT) positive signs are usually false.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: bedside ultrasound then diagnostic paracentesis if new/unexplained; absent flank dullness: clinically significant ascites unlikely, pursue other causes.

estimates.population: Hospitalized adults with suspected ascites, broad spectrum (Durham VA); n not stated in abstract

sources.citation: Williams JW Jr, Simel DL. The rational clinical examination. Does this patient have ascites? How to divine fluid in the abdomen. JAMA. 1992;267(19):2645-2648.
Simel DL, Halvorsen RA Jr, Feussner JR. Quantitating bedside diagnosis: clinical evaluation of ascites. J Gen Intern Med. 1988;3(5):423-428.
Cattau EL Jr, Benjamin SB, Knuff TE, Castell DO. The accuracy of the physical examination in the diagnosis of suspected ascites. JAMA. 1982;247(8):1164-1166.
Cummings S, Papadakis M, Melnick J, Gooding GA, Tierney LM Jr. The predictive value of physical examinations for ascites. West J Med. 1985;142(5):633-636.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use to exclude ascites in obese patients or when suspicion of SBP is high; ultrasound is required.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: New ascites with fever, abdominal pain or encephalopathy: paracentesis within hours to exclude SBP; tense ascites with oliguria: consider abdominal compartment/hepatorenal physiology.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Three-examiner study (Cattau 1982) showed overall accuracy of only 58% for physical manoeuvres in equivocal ascites; agreement is examiner-dependent.

extraction_notes: All numeric estimates come from the abstract of Simel 1988 (PMID 3049966): fluid wave LR+ 9.6, shifting dullness LR+ 5.76, absent bulging flanks LR- 0.12, absent peripheral edema LR- 0.17 (order of estimates: fluid wave, shifting dullness, bulging flanks absent, peripheral edema absent). No CIs, sensitivities or specificities are given in the abstract and the JGIM full text is not accessible, so those fields are null; reference standard is not stated in the abstract. The 1992 RCE (PMID 1573754) pooled table is not viewable (no abstract, publisher blocked), so its pooled LRs are not reported. Cattau 1982 (PMID 7057606, 21 patients, ultrasound reference) reports only ranges (sensitivity 50-94%, specificity 29-82%) and that absence of flank dullness is the one finding with >90% accuracy for excluding ascites; no per-manoeuvre numbers in the abstract. Cummings 1985 (PMID 3892916, 90 men with liver disease, sonography reference) reports positive predictive values only (shifting dullness 51%, fluid wave 73%; 96% for fluid wave when PT prolonged; 2% ascites when PT normal and no shifting dullness) - PPVs cannot be entered as sens/spec/LR so are noted here only. Records exam_shifting_dullness and exam_ascites_flank_dullness_fluid_wave cover the same manoeuvres and share this evidence base.
